# the contributor audit of two precise tetrahedral rank-three exclusions

Sources:

- Section 6 of `candidate de0cd073e31eb7f8`;
- `candidate 8bce978d82ec174e`;
- `candidate 07a18d1e8e33ee50`.

Full read: **PASS for the current corrected versions and their stated scopes**. The raw-unit common-shift coefficient must be t_i^2 (1^T H_i v)/(3P_i); root independently caught the former missing factor of t_i, and Defect corrected it while constructing the exact verifier. The current formula has the correct scaling. The equal-pair channel has zero shift by symmetry, but the general motion requires the corrected formula.

## Three full rows with two equal centroid pairs

If all coordinates are central, the joint index excludes the configuration immediately. Otherwise the two noncentral coordinates coincide and belong to the same side of every section. A triangular section cannot have two noncentral coordinates, so every cut is a strict quadrilateral of that same unoriented split.

The two exact centroid-difference factorizations force at least one diagonal pair to be equal. If the central pair were unequal, the other pair would be equal and its remaining equation would force the purportedly central coordinates above 1/3, a contradiction. Setting the central diagonal pair to one leaves the single symmetric plane and, only for 1/3<A<3/8, exactly two asymmetric planes. The discriminant and endpoint coalescence are accounted for.

Rank three requires all three distinct planes. Their unique linear relation fixes their relative scales and orientations up to global reversal. The reversed orientation has two central captured pairs and violates the index bound. The other orientation is exactly the previously audited positive-funding family. Threshold stationarity and the column sum fix its common scale, while the weighted-gradient equations fix its weights up to a common factor. The fourth row stays zero in the improving path, so its objective weight is irrelevant. This proves the entire stated pair-symmetric stratum, without a symmetry reduction for arbitrary b.

## Two full rows and a one-zero row

The one-zero-row multiplier formula gives z_j=w/b_j and the exact signed column-margin balance. A cap capturing the unique noncentral hole cannot be triangular, because the other triangular-section centroid coordinates are at most 1/3 and a full-row minimum cannot capture only one vertex. Its two excluded coordinates force the other row to capture them. If the other cut were triangular, its explicit complement-of-vertex row formula and the column sums would force the first row to capture only the hole. Thus both sections are strict complementary quadrilaterals. All vertex-contact cases are explicitly eliminated, not perturbed away.

For the joint motion, summing the three row perturbations gives zero exactly; the zero row retains its zero coordinate. Radial Hessian terms vanish by degree-one homogeneity. The corrected full-row curvature is -v^T H_i v/(3f_i), and the exact zero-row geometric-mean Hessian gives the retained penalty C. Maximizing the resulting quadratic -A alpha^2+B beta^2-C(alpha+beta)^2 gives the criterion B>AC/(A+C). Neither the threshold loss nor the zero-row loss is omitted.

When the other two central coordinates agree, the archived diagonal ordering identity forces their raw heights to agree in each plane. The exact centroid formulas then reduce to the two T roots in (1/2,1). Their coefficient relations determine b0 and a0-c0 with the positive square-root branch. The actual column equations, not arbitrary independent sections, determine the relative scaling. Substitution gives the displayed reciprocal-gap factorization.

Its sign proof is complete: both J factors are positive by the central-pair theorem; the squared factor is strictly positive from v>0 and zeta<3; the remaining quadratic in zeta is negative at both ends of its allowed interval and is convex. Hence it is negative throughout, making the full gap strictly positive. Equality b_j=1/3 is permitted. The unequal other-pair case is not inferred from this factorization.

The exact symbolic verifier checks nine identities, including the corrected raw-unit Schur shift. The expanded three-full-family verifier also checks the centroid factorizations and global support payment. These checks verify the displayed algebra; the geometric and sign arguments above are the proof.
